items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Professor Minetta's told us about those. He played at the tuxedo dance hall and some of the houses and all too. Yes. Yes. He's told us all about that.

ctx.x: Yeah. And of course, like those fellows would be the... Now as far as jazz is concerned, I used to play a lot of jazz on the piano, you know? Oh yes. But I never did fancy very much of piling up in those... the red light districts. I never said to go around there. I didn't want to worry about that at all. Although, much of my colleagues used to play. Piku and all of them used to play.
Professor Minetta's told us about those. He played at the tuxedo dance hall and some of the houses and all too. Yes. Yes. He's told us all about that. But I used to play for private people.

Private dancers I used to play. And I had a whole set of... a whole set of dances. During those ten days, they used to have a certain order of dances, you see? They start off with a waltz, you see? Then they did a polka, you see? Then a mizooka, then a shardis. They used to dance those kind of dances before and then come back to a polka and repeat that. And then they would have a waltz and quadrille. And when the waltz was danced, as the rule, the dancers used to get their partner for the quadrille to make sure…
